name: Meta
tagline: Two fast coding problems per round, think out loud, then fix bugs

values.name: Move fast
values.meaning: Build and learn quickly with urgency, together in one direction.

values.name: Build awesome things
values.meaning: Ship work that is inspiring, not just useful.

values.name: Be direct and respect your colleagues
values.meaning: Have hard conversations openly and respectfully.

values.name: Focus on long-term impact
values.meaning: Pick problems with lasting impact over quick wins.

values.name: Live in the future
values.meaning: Build the future you want and adopt it early.

values.name: Meta, Metamates, me
values.meaning: Own the mission and look after teammates.

loop.focus: 5 min intro, 30-35 min on one or two coding problems, 5 min Q&A.
Same format as the screen with a stricter bar.
Past projects, conflict, feedback, and fit with a fast pace.

behavioral_themes: Project you are most proud of
coding_style: One or two short DSA problems in about 35 minutes in CoderPad or a plain editor, no execution. Speed matters, so start brute force, talk through it, get working code, then optimize. Graded on reasoning, using hints, finding your own bugs, and stating big-O.
rubric: Working code beats an unfinished optimal idea
question_themes: Hash map counting and subarray sums
Merge or iterate k sorted lists

panel_flavor.manager: Maya asks about the project you are proudest of and its long-term impact, and how fast you shipped it.
panel_flavor.tech: Theo gives two problems back to back and watches the clock; he expects you to spot your own bugs before he points at them.
panel_flavor.skeptic: Sol asks you to dry-run your code on an edge case and wants measured impact numbers for any project claim.
